_note: What Nana, Shige's daughter in Minamino, says when the farmer talks to her (Talk, README.md, Villagers): the first pick whose if holds names the lines, one of them by the day; gift_ lines answer a gift by its reaction, gift_items her own answers to a keepsake and to dishes. She has no hearts; by the village pond she has her own lines (map condition). Our own lines.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: I counted the petals on the mat. I got to forty and then a big wind came!

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: The drum goes BOM and my tummy goes BOM too! Does yours?

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Is there really a rabbit up there making mochi? Kota says yes. Papa says ask the moon.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: I'm staying up till midnight. I am! ...What time is it now?

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: You again! Are you following me? ...That's okay, you can.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: I'm busy! Very busy. This is important worm business.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Hi! I'm Nana! I live down in Minamino with my dad. He grows vegetables and talks to the dirt.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Do you have a cow? Kota says you might get a cow. Can I name it?

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Kota says there's a fish in here as big as a dog. I'm going to see it first.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Kota caught three and I caught zero. It's not fair. The fish like him better.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Dad says no running to the pond in the rain. So I'm building a castle out of cushions.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: I caught a cicada this morning! I let it go. It was very loud about it.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: I made a snow jizo by the lane! Granny Kiku gave it a red scarf.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: I pull weeds for Dad in the morning. One weed, one copper. I'm going to be rich.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Granny Kiku lets me pick persimmons, but only the ones she says. The others are for drying.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Did you know the jizo by the lane watches over kids? So I'm extra safe down there.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: I found wild garlic by the little shrine! It smells like Dad's boots. But a good smell. Sort of.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Mulberries up past Dad's top beds! My fingers go all purple. Dad says I look like I lost a fight with a plum.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Yam bulbils are like baby potatoes on a vine! There's some in the bamboo and past Dad's top beds. I keep them in my pockets.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: There's snow mushrooms by the pine at the bottom! Dad says they're called enoki. I call them snow mushrooms.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: For ME? Wow! This is the best thing anybody ever gave me. Ever!

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Ooh, thank you! I'm gonna show Kota.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Um. Thanks. What is it?

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Bleh. That's a grown-up thing. Dad can have it.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: That's just a rock! I have a whole pile of rocks already!

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Another one? Dad says I can only take one present a day. Rules are rules.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: A clay rabbit! It goes right next to my bed. Its name is Mochi. It just decided.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Sweet! Can I eat it now? Before supper? Don't tell Dad.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Yum! You cook better than Dad. Don't tell him that either.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Okay! I'll share it with Dad.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: It's got the bitter white stuff in it. I'll give it to Dad.
